hero.beat: I build web interfaces that are fast and easy to use.

about.label: About me
body: I’m a frontend developer based in Ankara, currently working at InspireIT. I started as an intern at Bilgeweb in 2019 and later spent over a year at GuruDesk working in frontend development.

I enjoy turning a design into a working product in the browser. I use React, Vue and Astro to build new interfaces and improve existing ones. That includes tracking down why a page is slow and fixing the cause.
I care about how an interface feels to use. I spend time getting the details right, from a page that works comfortably on a phone to the way a button responds or an animation comes to a stop.

items.name: Porch
items.stack: Next.js 16 · Supabase · Stripe · shadcn/ui · Cloudflare Workers
items.summary: Porch brings your links together on a personal page. Create an account, add your photo and links, choose a theme, and share a short address. A live phone preview shows your changes as you edit.
items.detail: I designed and developed Porch from the initial idea through to launch, using Next.js, Supabase and Stripe on Cloudflare Workers. The database enforces subscription limits, and only Stripe webhooks can change a plan. Public pages score 98 on mobile Lighthouse.
items.alt: Dark theme, desktop: The Porch home page: the headline “One link for everything you make” beside three phones showing link-in-bio pages.
items.altMobile: Light theme, mobile: A Porch public page on a phone: a potter’s profile with a featured link and four more.

items.name: Parley
items.summary: Parley is an AI chat app that presents weather forecasts and calculation results as cards. It returns exact answers to calculations, and you can read replies as they are generated.
items.detail: I designed and built it with Nuxt 4 and Nuxt UI. It runs entirely on Cloudflare’s free tier, with Turnstile, signed sessions and rate limits to protect the AI quota from bot traffic.
items.stack: Nuxt 4 · Nuxt UI · AI SDK · Workers AI · TypeScript
items.alt: Dark theme, desktop: Parley answering a question about the weather in Istanbul with a forecast card and a calculation card.
items.altMobile: Light theme, mobile: Parley on a phone, showing the local time in Tokyo.

items.name: InspireIT
items.summary: The Turkish and English website for InspireIT, where I work. The company has provided data, cloud and IT infrastructure services to enterprise clients since 2003.
items.detail: I handled frontend development for the site, with dedicated pages for each product and industry. It uses WordPress and Elementor with a custom theme and plugins built for the site.
items.stack: WordPress · Elementor · PHP · custom theme and plugins
items.alt: The InspireIT home page: a headline about digital transformation next to a grid of four diamond-shaped images.
items.altMobile: The InspireIT home page on a phone.

items.name: Formadaş
items.stack: Nuxt 4 · Nuxt UI · TypeScript · SQLite · Wikidata
items.summary: Who has played for both Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe? Formadaş finds the players two clubs have in common, with their seasons, appearances and goals. Search by country and club, explore player careers and share their profiles. You can also install it on your phone.
items.detail: I built the app with Nuxt 4 and Nuxt UI. It caches Wikidata and API-Football data in SQLite and falls back to a local player index when live sources are unavailable. I improved the mobile experience with an installable app, player-specific share cards and preloaded photos.
items.alt: Dark theme, desktop: Formadaş comparing Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe, with a table of shared players, seasons, appearances and goals.
items.altMobile: Light theme, mobile: Emre Belözoğlu’s Formadaş profile, with his photo, career statistics, player details and a share button.
